runs.t: Recursion solves a problem by invoking the same operation on smaller instances. Dynamic programming reuses solutions to overlapping subproblems through memoization or bottom-up tables.
Define a termination condition and decreasing measure for recursion. For DP, identify state, transition, base cases and evaluation order; analyze the number of distinct states and transition costs.
A nested category tree can be traversed recursively, while computing the minimum cost to reach each step in a workflow can use DP when paths overlap repeatedly.
Deep recursion may overflow the call stack. DP consumes memory and only helps when subproblems overlap; simpler iterative algorithms are often easier for straightforward tasks.
